A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLM model-inversion study, with matching authors, datasets, attack strategies, and experiments. The main text and complete appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments on three VLMs, human evaluations, a confidence-threshold ablation, and repeated-seed results.

after.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction experiments on four VLMs, human evaluations, prompt-variation experiments, attention-map analyses, and repeated-seed results.

M1.justification: SMI-AW changes fundamentally despite retaining its name. V1 selects low-confidence tokens using a probability threshold, with uniform weighting as a fallback; v2 weights tokens by normalized total visual attention (Equation 4 and Algorithm 4). TMI, TMI-C, SMI, and the three inversion losses are retained.

E1.justification: V2 adds two alternative identity-question phrasings on FaceScrub, extending tested input conditions (Table S.1). The private datasets, public generator datasets, and identity/breed reconstruction tasks remain unchanged. Additional models and human ratings on StanfordDogs do not introduce new dataset domains.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain TMI, TMI-C, and SMI alongside SMI-AW, with the same cross-entropy, max-margin, and logit-maximization losses. InternVL is an additional attack target, not a competing inversion method. No new external attack baseline is evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix 1 changes the reported inversion budget for MiniGPT-v2 and Qwen2.5-VL from 100 to 70 steps; LLaVA remains at 70. Added configurations include InternVL2.5-8B, publicly released MiniGPT-v2, alternative prompts, and a StanfordDogs human study reporting 960 participants. The principal metrics and candidate-selection procedures are retained.

E4.justification: The confidence-threshold sensitivity study is removed and replaced by prompt-variation testing in Table S.1. V2 adds substantial analyses of attention across tokens and inversion steps, including Figure 2 and Figures S.9–S.12 for four models. The existing text-match-rate analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions' Appendix 3.2 and Table S.2 report three runs with different random seeds and mean plus standard deviation for SMI and SMI-AW on LLaVA/FaceScrub. Updated SMI-AW means and deviations change results, not the uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: SMI-AW results change throughout the main and supplementary tables. For example, FaceScrub logit-loss AttAccM changes from 59.25% to 61.01%, while LLaVA/FaceScrub human accuracy changes from 75.31% to 56.93%. V2 adds InternVL, StanfordDogs human-evaluation, prompt-variation, and attention-analysis results, and replaces qualitative reconstructions. Changed weighting and some inversion budgets prevent interpreting these as isolated same-procedure performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 4 substantively replaces the piecewise confidence-threshold definition with normalized visual-attention weights, changing the mathematical weighting in Equation 5. No theorem or proof is added; the other principal objectives and loss formulas are retained, with loss definitions moved to the appendix.

C1.justification: V1 presents confidence-weighted SMI-AW within a suite of four attacks. V2 makes token visual grounding and attention-guided weighting a separate central contribution in the abstract and introduction, redefining the claimed methodological advance. The overarching claim that VLMs leak private visual information remains.

C2.justification: V1 motivates weighting through low-confidence tokens providing corrective feedback. V2 replaces this explanation with attention as a proxy for visually informative gradients and adds arguments about linguistic context, gradient instability, and conflicting token updates. It also interprets the new prompt results as robustness evidence; the stated domain limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 revises documented inversion budgets, removes the obsolete confidence-threshold setting, and adds an InternVL implementation reference. It newly states that code is provided in supplementary material, although attack-code availability is not established by the supplied PDFs. Hardware and candidate-selection details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds InternVL references, attention-related works supporting the new interpretation, and further VLM and inversion-defense citations. The appendix's related-work discussion and positioning as the first study of inversion attacks on multimodal VLMs remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and contribution framing are extensively rewritten around attention-guided inversion. SMI-AW becomes a standalone main section, inversion-loss design moves to the appendix, and the analysis section is substantially expanded and reorganized.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned to incorporate attention analysis, and new attention-map figures appear throughout the paper and appendix. Qualitative reconstruction panels are replaced and expanded. The CelebA and StanfordDogs tables are merged, and table formatting, captions, and figure placement are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: The prompt-robustness test, fourth target architecture, and human evaluation on dogs modestly strengthen empirical validation. Attention visualizations clarify the revised method's motivation. The gains are limited by unspecified attention aggregation across layers/heads and by method and budget changes that prevent clean before-and-after performance comparisons.
